title: Seller sprint pocket battleplan — technical rapid enablement (draft)
summary: A compact, 8-slide pocket battleplan for sellers and SEs to run 10–15 minute technical calls that convert pilot conversations into commitment. Focus is on rapid qualification, engineering-friendly objections, economic fallback lanes (cost/latency), and a canary checklist for early pilots. Informal tone, includes quick scripts and triage matrix for live calls.
audience: SDRs, AEs, SEs, platform sellers, solution architects — anyone doing short technical discovery calls or pilot kickoffs.
objectives: Arm sellers with a 90s intro + 2 minute technical elevator
Provide a 3-step qualifier for infra/ops risk and cost concerns
Offer clear fallback options (model variant, dedicated vs hosted, latency tier) with economics language
Give an on-call style canary checklist to propose during pilot negotiation
slides_outline:
Title + TL;DR: 90s intro for sellers
- One line positioning: Redwood = predictable inference for production teams
- Value hooks: lower per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs; same API across hosted/dedicated/private
- Call to action: propose pilot with defined success metrics

Who we help (micro-segments)
- Platform teams: standardize inference across products
- Product teams: need fast time-to-value and predictable latency
- Regulated customers: private deployments and KMS integrations
- Quick qualifier: does the customer need <100ms p50 or deterministic throughput?

The 2-minute technical elevator (script)
- 0:00–0:30: runtime + routing summary (GPU runtime, batching, smart routing)
- 0:30–1:00: ops guarantees (SLAs, observability, rollouts)
- 1:00–2:00: fallback levers: quantized variants, dedicated reserved pools, regional routing

Rapid risk/impact qualifier (three screens)
- Data compliance: PII/regulated? -> Private (VPC) or on-prem
- Latency sensitivity: sub-100ms vs bursty throughput? -> Dedicated or tuned batching
- Cost tolerance: predictable spend vs pay-as-you-go? -> Reserved capacity vs hosted

Fallback economics cheat (phrases and numbers)
- "If latency is priority": recommend dedicated GPU pool + small reserved commit (estimates: X% cheaper per token at steady throughput)
- "If cost is priority": try quantized variant + cache/prefix strategy (expected token spend reduction: Y–Z%)
- Quick line: "We can run a two-week pilot with a capped spend and production-like routing — you get real numbers by day 3."

Canary / pilot checklist (propose on call)
- Goal: validate 3 metrics in 14 days: latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, functional quality on 10 prompts
- Resources: test model variants, enable KV caching, set up tracing hooks
- Rollback: automatic fallback to safe model variant if latency > SLA

Common objections + micro-scripts
- "We host everything internally": "We support private VPC/on-prem; many customers start hosted and move to private with identical APIs."
- "Cost is too high": "Let's baseline your current token spend vs a conservative quantized profile; we can cap pilot spend."
- "We need certified models": "We have Redwood-verified performance profiles and can run evaluation harnesses with your prompts."

Next steps (seller play)
- Ask for 10-minute access with an infra/contact to run 1-day smoke test
- Offer pilot template (14-day canary) and attach cost cap
- Capture success metrics and schedule 30-min wrap with engineering to propose commit
speaker_notes: Notes to sellers: keep the opening tight — use the 90s intro verbatim until you sense a technical gate. Use the rapid risk qualifier to identify the customer's dominant driver (latency, cost, compliance). If they say compliance first, jump straight to private options and KMS/HSM language. When cost objections arise, avoid abstract percentages; instead offer to run a one-day smoke test and promise a capped pilot spend. During pilot negotiation, insist on 3 measurable success metrics and a rollback policy. Use the linked artifacts (JIRA ticket for pilot, Confluence pilot template). Callouts: 1) avoid promising sub-50ms without benchmarking; 2) emphasize same API across modes to reduce engineering lift. Draft tone: conversational, leave TODO markers for PR/engineering owners.
